belief: If God loved me, I wouldn't be struggling.
origins: When money runs short, it is natural to wonder where God is. Many of us were taught, openly or quietly, that love and ease go together: good children are cared for, and loved people are comfortable. Hardship then feels like a message about how God sees us. Add a hard childhood, a loss, or a prayer that seemed unanswered, and the conclusion “He must not love me” can feel like the only explanation.
teaches: Scripture never ties God’s love to a smooth life. Jesus said plainly, “In the world you will have tribulation. But take courage; I have overcome the world!” Paul says that nothing in all creation can separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus. He also teaches that suffering produces perseverance, character, and hope, and that God has poured out His love into our hearts. The cross, where struggle and love met, is the proof of His love, not the absence of struggle.
self_statements: God must be angry with me.
Other people are not struggling like this, so God must love them more.
If God cared, He would fix this.
Maybe God does not love me the way He loves others.
I must have done something to lose His love.
My hardship proves I am not loved.
errors: Feeling unloved and concluding that I am.
Assuming I know how God feels about me from my circumstances.
Letting one hard season define God’s whole character.
Believing others are loved more because they struggle less.
questions: What did I learn growing up about the link between love and comfort?
Did Jesus, whom the Father loved, go through hardship? What does that tell me?
What does Scripture say can separate me from God’s love?
Where have I seen God’s care even in this hard season?
What evidence of God’s love do I have that does not depend on my bank account?
What would I say to a friend who believed this?
truth: God’s love for me is proven by Christ’s death for me, not by my circumstances. I can struggle and be deeply loved at the same time. Nothing, including a hard season with money, can separate me from His love.
hw_truths: God’s love is not measured by my comfort.
Nothing can separate me from His love.
Christ proved His love while I was still a sinner.
Hardship can grow perseverance, character, and hope.
I am loved in the middle of this.
log: Each day, write one sign of God’s love that has nothing to do with money, such as a person, a verse, or a moment of peace.
actions: Write the link you were taught.
Describe what you learned about love and comfort and who taught it.
Underline each thing that cannot separate you from God’s love.
Write five ways God has cared for you in this season.
Pray what you feel, including the hurt, and then ask Him to show His love.
prayer: Father, this season is hard and I have wondered whether You love me. Show me again that nothing can separate me from Your love in Christ. Hold me in this, and open my eyes to Your care. Amen.
hw_questions: What did I learn about love and comfort?
What does Romans 8 say can separate me from God’s love?
Where has God cared for me lately?
What did Jesus’ own life show about love and struggle?
What would I tell a friend?
What do I need to tell God honestly?
name_example: Sarah can write: “Nothing can separate me from God’s love, even this hard season.”
